{{Short description|Mathematical operation}}
In [[mathematics]], '''demonic composition''' is an operation on [[binary relation]]s that is similar to the ordinary [[composition of relations]] but is robust to refinement of the relations into ([[Partial function|partial]]) functions or [[injective relation]]s.

Unlike ordinary composition of relations, demonic composition is not [[Associative property|associative]].

==Definition==

Suppose <math>R</math> is a [[binary relation]] between <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> and <math>S</math> is a relation between <math>Y</math> and <math>Z.</math>  Their '''{{visible anchor|right demonic composition}}''' <math>R \textbf{;}^{\to} S</math> is a relation between <math>X</math> and <math>Z.</math>  Its graph is defined as
<math display=block>\{(x, z) \ : \ x \mathrel{(S \circ R)} z \text{ and for all } y \in Y \ (x \mathrel{R} y \text{ implies } y \mathrel{S} z)\}.</math>

Conversely, their '''{{visible anchor|left demonic composition}}''' <math>R \textbf{;}^{\leftarrow} S</math> is defined by
<math display=block>\{(x, z) \  : \ x \mathrel{(S \circ R)} z \text{ and for all } y \in Y \ (y \mathrel{S} z \text{ implies } x \mathrel{R} y)\}.</math>
